Note that we can rewrite this integral as

$$
{\int }_{0}^{6}\frac{40}{64-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{5}{8}{\int }_{0}^{6}\frac{1}{1-{(\frac{x}{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for the inverse hyperbolic tangent,

$$
\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{artanh}⁡u+C,
$$

the only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have ${(\frac{x}{8})}^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{x}{8}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{8}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=8\,\text{d}u.
$$

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from $x$ to $u.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\frac{3}{4}$ |

Using the above, we can now write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{6}\frac{40}{64-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5}{8}{\int }_{0}^{6}\frac{1}{1-{(\frac{x}{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{8}{\int }_{0}^{3/4}\frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\cdot 8\,\text{d}u \\  & =5{\int }_{0}^{3/4}\frac{\text{d}u}{1-{u}^{2}} \\  & =5\operatorname{artanh}⁡u\,{|}_{0}^{3/4} \\  & =5\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\frac{3}{4})-5\operatorname{artanh}⁡0 \\  & =5\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\frac{3}{4})\end{aligned}
$$
